task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: measurement of lineup coverage per possession
sample size for rare lineup configurations
evidence_establishes: No historical evidence was available; nothing was established by prior project studies.
evidence_does_not_establish: No historical evidence to assess; all aspects of the question remain open.
own_inferences: Within-team variation in lineup coverage is plausible because substitutions alter role composition, but the extent is unknown without data.
Coverage is likely correlated with average talent because skilled players often fill multiple roles, but the correlation is unlikely to be perfect, leaving room for partial separability.
Testing separability requires a well-defined performance outcome; the question omits one, so offensive efficiency is a natural candidate.
Role classification reliability is the greatest threat; misclassification could create spurious coverage signals or mask true variation.
uncertainties: Reliability and validity of organizer[path] role definitions from play-type data are unknown.
Base rate of coverage (>=1 of each role) is unknown; if very high or very low, power suffers.
Optimal talent proxy: single-year vs. multi-year, prior-season vs. same-season without lookahead.
Whether coverage varies enough within team after accounting for opponent and game state.
Whether the same players maintain consistent role labels across stints and seasons.

historical_effect.explanation: No earlier study-family records were found, so the decision is based solely on assessment of the current question and data.

blocking_constraints.text: Role definitions (organizer, shaper, terminal) depend on play-type classification with unknown reliability; if roles cannot be measured reliably, the whole construct is invalid.

If most NBA lineups inherently contain at least one of each role, the binary coverage indicator will have low within-team variance, requiring very large samples to detect effects conditional on talent.

prior_work.summary: No prior studies on this specific question were retrieved from the project's study-family records.

risks.text: Operator classification of players into organizer[path] roles from play-by-play and play-type data lacks published validation; random or systematic error in role assignment biases coverage and may create mechanical correlations with outcomes.
If the base rate of covered lineups is near 0 or 1 within some teams, the effective sample for within-team comparisons shrinks drastically, reducing power.

Lineup coverage may be correlated with opponent strength, game location, rest days, or score margin, all of which also affect offensive efficiency; failing to control them will produce confounded associations.

If talent proxies are estimated using data from the same season or future seasons, the control variable may absorb some of the variation that coverage would otherwise explain, yielding a biased estimate of partial association.

Terminal role is likely defined using shooting events that directly contribute to scoring; if offensive efficiency is the outcome, the role definition may induce a non-causal mechanical association with the outcome.
Exploring multiple outcomes (offensive rating, defensive rating, net rating) or multiple coverage definitions without pre-specification and correction inflates false positive rates.

Clustering at the team-season and stint level, along with multiple control variables, reduces effective degrees of freedom; although 420k possessions exist, the number of independent within-team coverage shifts may be modest.
The base rate of coverage influences the standard error of the coverage coefficient; extreme base rates reduce power for a given sample size.

design.estimand: Partial association between lineup structural-role coverage (binary: roster has at least one organizer, one shaper, one terminal on the floor) and offensive efficiency (points per 100 possessions), conditional on average player talent, within NBA team-seasons.
design.unit: Lineup stint (uninterrupted 5-man unit) or individual possession; primary analyses at the stint level aggregated from possessions.
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff stints from the 2022-23 through 2025-26 NBA seasons, excluding garbage time (score differential >20 points in the 4th quarter with under 2 minutes remaining) and stints shorter than three possessions.
design.power: Expected power > 0.80 to detect a partial R² increment of 0.002 for coverage beyond talent controls, assuming at least 15,000 within-team coverage changes across the sample; sensitivity analyses to quantify power under varying base rates.
design.controls: Five-player average talent (pre-season multi-year regularized adjusted plus-minus or equivalent prior-only metric), home/away, rest days, opponent defensive rating (prior season), score margin at stint start, and team-season fixed or random intercepts.
design.falsification: Random permutation of role labels within player-season should destroy the coverage coefficient; coverage should not predict opponent offensive talent after controlling for own defense; coverage defined using irrelevant categories (e.g., height terciles) should show no effect.
design.multiplicity: Primary test on offensive efficiency; exploratory tests on defensive rating and net rating, with Bonferroni-Holm correction across the two secondary outcomes.
design.decision_rule: Linear mixed model with team-season random intercepts; primary coefficient significant at p < 0.01; consistent direction and significance across alternative talent metrics and role classification thresholds; report 95% confidence intervals.
design.data_version: Data fixed as of 2026-07-13, covering complete NBA regular seasons and playoffs from 2022-23 through 2025-26, sourced from NBA stats API play-by-play, substitutions, matchups, box scores, and derived play-type possession records.
